pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.body: The SMS cron's deleteMany OR branch matches solely on retryCount > 1 with no method, scheduled, or cancelled scoping, so it can permanently delete non-SMS reminders (including future-dated email/WhatsApp reminders) that this handler does not own, silently dropping those notifications.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cross-method data deletion: the SMS cron deletes workflow reminders belonging to other delivery methods once their retryCount exceeds 1.
raw_findings.impact: The SMS cron's deleteMany OR branch matches solely on retryCount > 1 with no method, scheduled, or cancelled scoping, so it can permanently delete non-SMS reminders (including future-dated email/WhatsApp reminders) that this handler does not own, silently dropping those notifications.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new OR branch in the deleteMany where-clause omits the method filter that the sibling branch and every other cron's delete query include.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Scope the second OR branch to this handler's rows: add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`) alongside the `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition.
raw_findings.title: retryCount delete condition not scoped to SMS method, so SMS cron can delete reminders of other methods
raw_findings.trigger: Any WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, or SMS) acquires retryCount > 1 — e.g. once the same retry pattern is added to the WhatsApp/email crons, or a row is updated by any other code path — and the SMS cron endpoint runs its opening deleteMany.

raw_findings.body: The catch block increments retryCount for every error indiscriminately; after two transient failures the deleteMany at the top of the next run permanently deletes the reminder, so a valid SMS with a correct phone number is never sent even after the outage or rate limit clears.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Legitimate scheduled SMS reminders are silently and permanently dropped after brief provider outages or rate limiting.
raw_findings.impact: The catch block increments retryCount for every error indiscriminately; after two transient failures the deleteMany at the top of the next run permanently deletes the reminder, so a valid SMS with a correct phone number is never sent even after the outage or rate limit clears.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new retry counter treats all exceptions from the scheduling path as permanent failures without classifying error type.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only count permanent, non-retryable failures (e.g. Twilio invalid-number error codes) toward retryCount, or raise the deletion threshold and skip incrementing on known-transient errors such as rate-limit and network exceptions.
raw_findings.title: Transient failures (rate limit, Twilio outage) count toward retryCount and permanently delete valid reminders
raw_findings.trigger: twilio.scheduleSMS throws for a transient reason — checkSMSRateLimit throwing on a monthly rate limit, a temporary Twilio/network outage, or missing env credentials — on two consecutive cron executions for the same reminder.

raw_findings.body: Both writers set retryCount to the same stale value + 1, losing an increment; a reminder that failed on both runs still shows retryCount 1, delaying deletion and causing extra failed scheduling attempts beyond the intended two.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Lost updates under concurrent cron executions make the retry cap ineffective for that run.
raw_findings.impact: Both writers set retryCount to the same stale value + 1, losing an increment; a reminder that failed on both runs still shows retryCount 1, delaying deletion and causing extra failed scheduling attempts beyond the intended two.
raw_findings.root_cause: The counter update is computed from an in-memory value fetched at the start of the run rather than atomically in the database.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic update `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` in both the else branch and the catch block instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1`.
raw_findings.title: retryCount incremented via non-atomic read-modify-write instead of Prisma increment
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping cron invocations (e.g. a slow run exceeding the cron interval, or a manual trigger concurrent with the schedule) both read the same reminder's retryCount before either writes.

raw_findings.body: The exception thrown by the update inside the catch handler is uncaught, so the for-loop aborts, all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behavior of merely logging and continuing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A single stale reminder row turns a previously-logged error into an unhandled exception that halts the whole cron batch.
raw_findings.impact: The exception thrown by the update inside the catch handler is uncaught, so the for-loop aborts, all remaining unscheduled reminders in this run are skipped, and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the previous behavior of merely logging and continuing.
raw_findings.root_cause: New awaited database write added inside a catch handler without its own error handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the retryCount update in the catch block in its own try/catch (or use updateMany, which does not throw on zero matches) so a failed bookkeeping write cannot abort processing of the remaining reminders.
raw_findings.title: prisma update inside catch block is unguarded and can abort the entire cron loop
raw_findings.trigger: A reminder fetched by findMany is deleted concurrently (e.g. its booking is cancelled and handleCancelBooking removes its workflow reminders) before scheduling fails and the catch block runs its update, which then throws Prisma P2025 (record not found).

raw_findings.body: Every pending SMS reminder for the locked account reaches retryCount 2 within two cron runs and is deleted by the next run's deleteMany; if the lock is later lifted (e.g. a false-positive spam lock is reviewed), the reminders are already gone and cannot be sent.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Reversible administrative lock state causes irreversible deletion of otherwise valid workflow reminders.
raw_findings.impact: Every pending SMS reminder for the locked account reaches retryCount 2 within two cron runs and is deleted by the next run's deleteMany; if the lock is later lifted (e.g. a false-positive spam lock is reviewed), the reminders are already gone and cannot be sent.
raw_findings.root_cause: The else branch treats every falsy return from scheduleSMS as a scheduling failure, but scheduleSMS also returns undefined for the deliberate, potentially reversible SMS-lock state.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish the lock case from a genuine scheduling failure — e.g. have scheduleSMS signal 'locked' distinctly and skip the retryCount increment (or skip locked reminders in the query) so reminders survive a temporary lock.
raw_findings.title: SMS-lock state increments retryCount and leads to permanent deletion of a locked account's reminders
raw_findings.trigger: A user or team is temporarily in SMSLockState.LOCKED: twilio.scheduleSMS returns undefined (its early return on isLockedForSMSSending), so the else branch runs on two consecutive cron executions.

raw_findings.body: The new data-destructive behavior — incrementing retryCount on failure and permanently deleting reminders once retryCount > 1 — ships unverified; a regression could either delete reminders prematurely or reintroduce the infinite-retry loop this PR fixes, and CI would not catch it.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regressions in retry counting or the deletion threshold would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.impact: The new data-destructive behavior — incrementing retryCount on failure and permanently deleting reminders once retryCount > 1 — ships unverified; a regression could either delete reminders prematurely or reintroduce the infinite-retry loop this PR fixes, and CI would not catch it.
raw_findings.root_cause: Behavioral change with irreversible data deletion introduced without any accompanying automated test.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an integration test for the scheduleSMSReminders handler that mocks twilio.scheduleSMS to fail, asserts retryCount is incremented on the failing reminder, and asserts a reminder with retryCount > 1 is deleted on the next invocation while retryCount <= 1 reminders survive.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage for new retryCount increment and retry-based deletion behavior
raw_findings.trigger: Any future refactor of the SMS cron (e.g. changing the deleteMany filter, the retry threshold, or the else/catch bookkeeping) is merged without a regression check.

validated_findings.trigger: Any future refactor of the SMS cron (e.g. changing the deleteMany filter, the retry threshold, or the else/catch bookkeeping) is merged without a regression check.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap observation, not a functional defect. The absence of tests is a quality concern but does not constitute a bug introduced by the patch. Stylistic/process findings are excluded.
